note: Every network source this recipe touches, with the digest verified at fetch time. No credentials appear anywhere in this file or in the built image.

base_image.note: Docker's linux/386 platform on an amd64 host needs no binfmt/QEMU emulation: the host CPU executes 32-bit x86 instructions natively, only the userland ABI (dpkg arch i386) differs. Confirmed with `docker run --rm --platform=linux/386 debian:bookworm-slim dpkg --print-architecture` -> i386.

requirement_evidence.conclusion: The current manifest pairs BCF format 3.11 with Biber 2.22. This VM's Biber 2.21 receipt belongs to an earlier browser release and must not be used with the current release.
requirement_evidence.local_texlive_2025_cross_check: The developer machine's TeX Live 2025 (nixos.org build) also ships biblatex with \blx@bcfversion{3.11}; this cross-check documents the old VM pairing, not current-release compatibility.

a_debian_bookworm_package.detail: `apt-cache policy biber` inside the i386 bookworm-slim container reports candidate 2.18-1, older than the required 2.21.

b_texlive_i386_linux_binary.detail: TeX Live 2026's dated historic snapshot repository (https://texlive.info/historic/systems/texlive/2026/tlnet-final/) returns 404 as of this build (2026 has not been archived as a historic/final year yet). The current rolling mirror (https://mirror.ctan.org/systems/texlive/tlnet/) still ships an i386-linux biber binary but its texlive.tlpdb gives no exact upstream version number and would not be reproducible (it moves). TeX Live 2025's frozen tlnet-final repository ships biber.i386-linux revision 75738, and `biber --version` from that archive reports exactly 2.21. Used this: pinned, historic, verified by digest at fetch time.

c_cpan.detail: Option (b) succeeded, so CPAN/Perl compilation (slowest, largest guest) was not attempted.

download.note: The build extracts bin/i386-linux/biber from this archive on the HOST (bookworm-slim ships no xz-utils, and installing one merely to unpack once would add unnecessary guest-image bloat) and COPYs the plain 32-bit ELF executable into the image.
download.runtime_dependencies: ldd inside an i386 bookworm-slim container: linux-gate.so.1 (vDSO), libpthread.so.0, libc.so.6, /lib/ld-linux.so.2 -- all already present in debian:bookworm-slim. No Perl, no fontconfig, no CA certificates, no additional libraries were installed.

v86_runtime.note: The emulator and runtime files, pinned per file by URL, size and SHA-256; prepare.mjs refuses any byte that disagrees. copy.sh publishes unversioned builds, so the digests are the pin. recipe_pin is the rstudio/tinytex revision the original evaluation recipe was derived from, kept for the record only.
v86_runtime.licence_evidence: libv86.js top-of-file header and https://github.com/copy/v86/blob/master/LICENSE both state BSD-2-Clause.

licences.debian_base_image: various OSI licences per Debian package (no packages beyond the base bookworm-slim rootfs are installed in the guest)
licences.biber: Artistic-2.0 (confirmed via https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plk/biber/dev/README.md: 'modify it under the terms of the Artistic License 2.0')
licences.perl: not shipped in the guest -- the Biber TeX Live binary is self-contained and requires no Perl interpreter at runtime
